title: How to Make Your AI Agent Smarter Without Training a New Model — Thinking Tokens, Thinking Budgets and JSON Field Order #shorts
caption:
ENGINEERING · How do you make your AI agent smarter without training a new model? Make it think longer.

Your AI travel agent booked a 40-minute connection across terminals. The customer missed the flight.

The agent had every fact it needed. It just answered in one go. The first flight lands at 2:00 in Terminal 1, the next leaves at 2:40 from Terminal 3, and the transfer takes an hour. The first word it wrote was "book".

Every word a model writes gets one pass through the model. To think more, it has to write more. Write each check before the answer, and 40 minutes fails against an hour.

Thinking isn't free, though. Thinking tokens are billed as output, so a 300-token reply with 6,000 tokens of thinking costs 21 times the output, on every call.

3 rules for any AI agent that makes decisions:

1. Turn thinking on where the answer needs steps, and off where it needs a fact. For a travel agent, that's the connection check.
2. Set a thinking cap per route, not the maximum the model allows.
3. When thinking is off, put the reasoning field before the answer field in your JSON. Otherwise the agent picks "book: yes" first and writes the reason after.

Thinking adds steps, not facts. If the agent has the wrong transfer time, it checks the wrong number very carefully.

Save this for your next prompt review. Send it to whoever owns your agent's JSON schema.
